column5: Cao Zhen, a burly grand general of Wei in heavy armor, twisting in the saddle of a galloping horse to loose an arrow.
Cao Xiu, a young cavalry general of Wei, leaning far forward on a galloping horse with his spear leveled.
Xiahou Shang, a Wei general directing a night river raid, torch raised in one hand, cloak blowing.
Xiahou Ba, a fierce young general, one foot on a rock, raising his saber with a roar.
Cao Zhi, a poet prince, striding forward with a wine cup in one hand and a writing brush in the other, sleeves flying.
Zhu Huan, a proud general of Wu, standing on a fortress wall with arms crossed, laughing at a vast enemy host below.
Zhu Ran, a short but fierce general of Wu, defending a city wall with sword drawn, pointing forward.
Ding Feng, a veteran of Wu who has thrown off his armor, charging bare-armed through falling snow with a short blade.
Quan Cong, a general of Wu standing on the prow of a warship, pointing ahead with a command flag.
Bu Zhi, a calm scholar-general of Wu in a plain robe, holding a scroll and a walking staff on a riverbank.
Wutugu, a giant barbarian king covered in woven rattan armor, lifting a huge club over his shoulder.
King Mulu, a southern chieftain riding an elephant and ringing a bell, a tiger running alongside.
King Duosi, a cunning southern chieftain in a feathered headdress, grinning beside a steaming poisonous spring.
Mangyachang, a fierce southern warrior riding a great ox, swinging a huge broad-bladed polearm.
Kebineng, a steppe chieftain in furs and a fur hat, drawing a composite bow from the back of a steppe horse.
Guan Suo, a handsome young warrior with a flower-patterned headband, whirling a long glaive.
Zhou Cang, a dark-faced burly retainer with a curly beard, carrying a great crescent blade on his shoulder, glaring loyally.
Elder Qiao, a dignified white-bearded gentleman with a walking cane, smiling proudly.
Chen Jiao, an upright minister of Wei holding a ceremonial tablet in both hands, stern-faced.
Cui Yan, an imposing official with a magnificent very long beard, standing tall with his hands behind his back.
Li Tong, a chivalrous commander leading a night river crossing, shield raised against arrows.
Sun Yi, a hot-tempered young lord of the Sun clan, drawing his sword with a fierce shout.
Guan Hai, a rebel chieftain with a yellow headscarf, brandishing a great saber on horseback.
Fu Tong, a general fighting to the last, surrounded, gripping a broken spear and shouting defiance.
Yang Yi, a sharp-tongued staff officer with an impatient scowl, counting rods in one hand and a ledger scroll in the other.
Pan Jun, a stern provincial official pointing an accusing finger, a scroll of charges in his other hand.
Liao Hua, a weathered veteran general with graying temples, breaking out on horseback with spear in hand.
Sun Qian, an affable envoy in a traveling cloak, bowing slightly with a letter held in both hands.
Mi Fang, a nervous garrison commander with his helmet under his arm, looking back over his shoulder.
Cai Mao, a naval commander on the deck of a warship, pointing with a command baton, sails behind him.
Li Hui, a clever official-general of the south riding hard as an envoy, cloak streaming, a confident smile.
Deng Zhi, a bold envoy walking calmly past a boiling cauldron, laughing.
Zhang Ni, a tough frontier general with a bandaged arm and a short sword, steady gaze, mountains behind.
Jia Kui, a stern governor-general standing on a river dike, a law scroll in one hand and a sword at his side.
Tian Yu, a frugal northern frontier general on horseback, directing wagons into a circle against nomad riders.
Qian Zhao, a frontier commander facing down mounted nomads, bow in hand and arm outstretched.
Lu Fan, an elegant general of Wu in fine robes over armor, placing a stone on a go board with a smile.
Ling Cao, a daring vanguard officer charging ahead in a light boat, sword raised.
Zhu Zhi, an elder statesman-general of Wu with a gray beard, leaning on his sword, kindly but stern.
Zhang Ji, a cavalry warlord of the northwest in fur-trimmed armor, leading riders through dust.
Fan Chou, a brawny cavalry general of the northwest, thrusting his spear from a charging horse.
Guo Tu, a scheming adviser whispering behind a feather fan, sly sidelong eyes.
Xin Ping, an anxious loyal adviser unrolling a map with knitted brows.
Chunyu Qiong, a drunken general with loosened armor, hugging a wine jar and laughing.
Gao Gan, an ambitious governor standing on a mountain pass, cloak in the wind, hand on his sword.
Yuan Shang, a handsome proud young heir in ornate armor, plumed helmet under his arm.
Cao Chun, commander of elite heavy cavalry in black lamellar armor, charging on a horse with a leopard-pelt saddle.
Wu Yi, a dignified steady general with his spear planted beside him, a banner behind.
Wu Lan, a bold vanguard officer charging on foot with saber and shield.
Leng Bao, a general breaking a river dike at night, torch in one hand and a spade in the other.
Ma Zhong, a genial general of the south, laughing heartily with one hand on his belt.
Sun Ben, an elder cousin of the Sun clan, a mounted general leading troops across a river under a banner.
Hu Zhen, an arrogant general of the northwest raising a whip and shouting orders.
Wu Anguo, a hero swinging a heavy iron hammer, one wrist bandaged.
Han Hao, a resolute officer with clenched teeth, sword pointed forward and shield on his arm.
Yan Pu, a prudent adviser in a Daoist cap, calmly sealing a granary door with a strip of paper.
Yang Feng, a bandit turned general escorting an imperial carriage, saber in hand.
Gongsun Kang, a cold-eyed northern lord in a fur-lined robe seated on a tiger skin, one hand on a lacquered box.
Zhang Miao, a generous gallant governor offering a wine cup with an open hand, conflicted eyes.
Chen Dao, a loyal guard commander with a white feather plume on his helmet, spear held at guard.
